What was disputed was never the work — it was a rebase conflict, held three times because the trunk hotfix e284ee7 added `pr_heads` to the same two lines of `plan_inputs` that this branch extends with `**_triage_facts`, so every correction round re-hit it. Both edits are additive; I kept both keys and the rebase onto 74497d9 is finished. Two findings are upheld and fixed in 9f1a7de: `plan_inputs` now reads the index through the same `plan_order.overlay` the wave applies, because `after` is a `DIGEST_FIELDS` name and `overlay` derives it — un-overlaid, `asf next` and the status cell would compute a different `card_digest` than the tick recorded at launch and call stale every Task whose order its plan derives, which is precisely what D3 forbids; and `row.common` is now read with `getattr` like `row.between` beside it. One finding is overruled and never returns: that `_triage_facts` is dead code is not a defect — `lifecycle.round_log` does not exist and `plan_rows` does not accept `stale_briefs` or `rounds` (asf/feeder/rows.py:798-800), so the guard is exactly what lets Task 6 land safely ahead of Tasks 1 and 2 rather than breaking every planner. What changes: the footprint is corrected down to Task 6's five files. Task 7's `asf/record/setfield.py` and `asf/tick/step_health.py` are not delivered on this branch — nothing in the diff touches them and `setfield.py` still has no ruling support — so holding them in T-0081's grant only makes T-0082 wait on T-0081 through `footprint.first_conflict` (asf/feeder/rows.py:608-613). Narrowing `writes:` releases T-0082 to its own lane, and this row closes.
